world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Etcho, G. 1988. Phonological interference between Nagot and English Language (thesis, Glottolog doctype phonology); not online. Kluge 2011 Ede survey is sociolinguistic only.

sources.citation: Durieux, Jude A., Evelin I. K. Durieux-Boon & Angela Kluge. 2011. A sociolinguistic survey of the Ede language communities of Benin and Togo, Volume 7: Northern Nago language area. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2011-008. Dallas: SIL International. 62 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (naming, location, RTT intercomprehension with Yoruba/Ife, vitality, attitudes, literacy). Only prosodic remark, p. 32 (sec. 5.3.3): the 1987 Yoruba New Testament 'would be easier to understand.. An additional advantage would be that tone is marked in this translation.' No word 'stress'/'accent' in a linguistic sense.

sources.citation: Kluge, Angela. 2011. A sociolinguistic survey of the Ede language communities of Benin and Togo, Introduction and Volume 1: Ede language family - Background and assessment methodology. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2011-002. xi+209 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 2 'Previous research' (pp. 11-12) lists no linguistic description at all for Manigri-Kambolé ('little linguistic research has been done outside the realm of standard Yoruba'; described varieties are Cabe, Ica, Idaca, Ife). Fn. 36 p. 81: 'Tone markings were transcribed but were not included in the analysis due to ambiguities in proper weighting.' Appendix L/O wordlists and phrase lists 'Nago (N) (Kambolé)' and 'Nago (N) (Manigri)' (elicited 1992-03-23/24) carry tone diacritics.
sources.venue: SIL Electronic Survey Report 2011-002. xi+209 pp

sources.citation: Ethnologue 16th ed. (2009) web entry 'Ede Nago, Manigri-Kambolé' [xkb] (the Internet Archive 2012-10-25) and OLAC combined catalog for xkb (the Internet Archive 2026-02-13)
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnologue: lexical similarity 87-91% with Ede Nago, 77% Yoruba (Porto-Novo), 78% Ife (Tchetti); SIL bibliography lists only the 1999 Abrégé and the 2011 survey vols 1 and 7. OLAC: the only 'language description' is the Glottolog page itself.

sources.citation: Kluge, Angela. 2007. A synchronic lexical study of the Ede language continuum of West Africa: The effects of different similarity judgment criteria. Afrikanistik online 2007. doi:10.18716/ojs/aaeo/2007_3518
sources.note: Nothing; lexicostatistics only (Manigri-Nago and Kambolé-Nago placed among southwestern Ede varieties).

sources.citation: Kohler, Anna. 1983. Le ton en ifè; Boëthius, Hélène. 1983. Description préliminaire des phonèmes segmentaux et types de syllabes ifè. In Nicole (ed.), Études linguistiques préliminaires dans quelques langues du Togo. Lomé: SIL. [closest described Ede neighbour, ifee1241, NOT this variety]
sources.note: For Ife (Tchetti): three level tones per syllable, no mention of accent/stress. Not a statement about Manigri-Kambolé; recorded only as the nearest described Ede variety (Ethnologue: 78% lexical similarity).
sources.venue: Études linguistiques préliminaires dans quelques langues du Togo

sources.note: The only phonological description Glottolog lists for xkb; a contrastive tone-language-vs-English study is very likely to state explicitly how Nagot prosody (tone) differs from English stress. Note the identity caveat: 'Nagot' in Benin often means Southern Nago (Kétou/Pobè), so its lect must be checked.
